_strings.@@abab9a685265: DC Earned Income Tax Credit (DC EITC) — filers WITH a qualifying child — DC residents who qualify for the federal Earned Income Credit and have a qualifying child — or who would qualify but for lacking an SSN (ITIN filers compute the federal EIC amount ignoring the SSN requirement). If married filing jointly, the taxpayer, spouse and qualifying child(ren) must each have an SSN or an IRS-issued ITIN; if the adults have SSNs/ITINs but the child(ren) do not, claim the DC EITC for filers WITHOUT a qualifying child instead. Cannot be claimed by a filer whose status is "Dependent claimed by someone else."
_strings.@@b0d21a60326b: Credit for Child and Dependent Care Expenses — DC full-year or statutory residents who claimed (or were eligible for) the federal child and dependent care credit on federal Form 2441 for the care of a qualifying dependent so the taxpayer could work or look for work. Part-year residents use DC Form D-2441 instead. A filer who did not file a federal return because they were below the federal filing threshold still completes federal Form 2441 and multiplies the result by .32.
_strings.@@c1fdb3acd5d7: Schedule H — Homeowner and Renter Property Tax Credit (circuit-breaker) — DC residents who owned or rented their DC home and were not claimed as a dependent (with an age-70 exception path). Renters' property tax is deemed = 20% of rent paid; homeowners use actual DC real property tax. One claim per tax filing unit; cannot claim for an exempt property owned by a government, house of worship, or nonprofit. Can be filed standalone (electronically via MyTax.DC.gov or by mail) if not required to file a D-40.
_strings.@@ced8055f8bcb: Treaty conformity — DC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from DC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the DC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: DC's Form D-40 begins from federal adjusted gross income (D-40 Line 4; Schedule I is titled "Additions to and Subtractions from Federal Adjusted Gross Income"), and DC's only mechanism for adding income back is Schedule I, Calculation A "Additions to federal adjusted gross income." The verified 2025 Schedule I Calculation A addition lines are: (1) part-year resident adjustment, (2) income distributions eligible for federal income averaging (Form 4972), (3) federal additional/bonus depreciation and extra IRC sec.179, (4) any part of a discrimination award subject to income averaging, (5) S-corporation deductions from Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S), (6) pass-through losses from DC unincorporated businesses exceeding the $12,000 threshold, (7) "Other. Attach a Calculation A, Line 7 Statement", and (8) capital gains deferred on the federal return due to investment in a Qualified Opportunity Fund. For 2025 the booklet ENUMERATES what belongs on the open-ended Line 7 "Other": interest on obligations of other states and their political subdivisions (new for 2025), capital gains on qualified small business stock, and the federal Schedule 1-A deductions DC disallows (tips, overtime, car-loan interest, enhanced senior deduction). None of these is treaty income, and the word "treaty" appears ZERO times in the entire 2025 D-40 booklet (re-counted this session over all 5,548 extracted lines). There is NO line that adds back income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty (contrast California's explicit Schedule CA treaty add-back). Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and DC has no treaty add-back, it flows through and is NOT re-taxed by DC. Therefore DC conforms (treaty-exempt income remains exempt).
_strings.@@cf3ee434644b: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): OBBBA NON-CONFORMITY — DC DECOUPLED FROM FEDERAL LAW: "In July 2025, the U.S. Congress passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA)... In November 2025, the D.C. Council passed a new law limiting the number of OBBBA tax changes that will affect District taxpayers." DC will NOT recognize the higher federal basic standard deduction, the tips / overtime / car-loan-interest deductions, the enhanced senior deduction, or the QSBS capital-gain exclusion. For 2025 the booklet ENUMERATES the open-ended Schedule I, Calculation A, Line 7 "Other" additions: interest on obligations of other states and their political subdivisions (NEW for 2025), capital gains on qualified small business stock, and the federal Schedule 1-A deductions DC disallows (tips, overtime, car-loan interest, enhanced senior deduction). DC AGI therefore diverges from federal AGI for far more filers than in 2024. Resolve via: Schedule I, Calculation A, Line 7 ("Other. Attach a Calculation A, Line 7 Statement") and its 2025 booklet instructions at the citation URL; the add-back amounts come from the filer's own federal return (Schedule 1-A tips/overtime/car-loan-interest/senior deduction, QSBS gain exclusion, out-of-state municipal bond interest).

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form D-40 Line 20: 'Tax' — instructions: 'If Line 19 is $100,000 or less, use the tax tables on pages 93-102 to determine your tax. If Line 19 is more than $100,000, use Calculation I on page 20.' Line 19 DC taxable income = Line 16 (DC adjusted gross income) minus Line 18 (DC deduction amount): 'Subtract Line 18 from Line 16. Enter the result; if a loss, fill in the oval.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 RATES UNCHANGED, verified THREE ways: the rate table is still the one 'For taxable years beginning January 1, 2022' — the booklet's Reminders print, the booklet's Calculation I/Tax Rate Schedule print (p. 20), and the live OTR 'DC Individual and Fiduciary Income Tax Rates' page ('The tax rates for tax years beginning after 12/31/2021 are') all read the same seven brackets and the same printed constants. DC has not changed individual income tax rates since TY2022. 2025 CHANGE — DC DECOUPLED ITS STANDARD DEDUCTION FROM FEDERAL LAW: 'Starting with tax year 2025, the District has established its own standard deduction amounts which are different from the federal standard deduction amounts' — $15,000 (single, dependent filers, married/RDP filing separately), $22,500 (head of household), $30,000 (married/RDP filing jointly, qualifying widow(er) with dependent children, and married/RDP filing separately on the same return), up from $14,600/$21,900/$29,200. This is NOT the 2024 pack's 'increasing based on the federal law' mechanism: the D.C. Council's November 2025 law explicitly refuses the OBBBA 'Higher federal basic standard deduction', so the 2025 DC amounts deliberately do NOT match the OBBBA federal figures. Base guidance: Supply 2025 Form D-40 Line 16, 'DC adjusted gross income, Line 7 minus Line 15.' Line 7 = Line 4 federal adjusted gross income (from the federal 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR) plus DC additions (Line 5 franchise tax deducted; Line 6 other additions from DC Schedule I, Calculation A, Line 9); Lines 8-14 are DC subtractions (taxable state/local refunds, taxable Social Security and tier 1 railroad retirement, income taxed on a DC franchise/fiduciary return, DC/federal government survivor benefits, unemployment insurance benefits, other Schedule I Calculation B subtractions). A filer with no DC additions or subtractions has DC AGI equal to federal AGI. The engine then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Line 18 for a standard-deduction filer) to reproduce Line 19 DC taxable income, and applies the rate schedule to reproduce Line 20. NEW FOR 2025: out-of-state municipal bond interest is a Schedule I Calculation A Line 7 addition, and the federal Schedule 1-A tips/overtime/car-loan-interest/enhanced-senior deductions must be added back — so DC AGI now diverges from federal AGI for more filers than in 2024. SINGLE RATE SCHEDULE FOR ALL FILING STATUSES: DC publishes one 'Income Tax Rate Table' (repeated as 'Calculation I/Tax Rate Schedule') that applies to Line 19 DC taxable income regardless of filing status; it is duplicated per status here. Married filing separately is NOT half of married filing jointly — every status uses the identical schedule. Only the standard deduction differs by status. PRINTED CONSTANTS VERIFIED EXACT (re-derived for 2025): $400 = 4% x $10,000; $2,200 = $400 + 6% x $30,000; $3,500 = $2,200 + 6.5% x $20,000; $19,650 = $3,500 + 8.5% x $190,000; $42,775 = $19,650 + 9.25% x $250,000; $91,525 = $42,775 + 9.75% x $500,000 — each printed '$X, plus Y% of the excess over $Z' constant equals the cumulative sum of the prior brackets with no rounding divergence. NO PERSONAL OR DEPENDENT EXEMPTIONS: the 2025 Form D-40 computes DC taxable income as Line 16 minus Line 18 only — there is no exemption line on the form, so this pack ships no exemption keys; test vectors use exemptions_count 0 and dependents_count 0. TAX TABLE MANDATE below $100,000: Form D-40 Line 20 and its instructions direct filers with Line 19 taxable income of $100,000 or less to 'use the tax tables on pages 93-102'; only above $100,000 is Calculation I (exact bracket math) used. The 2025 tables are built on $50 income bands, so bracket math can differ from the printed table by a dollar or two within a band (observed: the $25,000-$25,049 band prints $1,302 vs $1,300 of bracket math at exactly $25,000, and $61,100-$61,149 prints $3,595 vs $3,593.50) — the filed form must use the table when Line 19 is $100,000 or less. DEDUCTION TYPE MUST MATCH FEDERAL: Line 17 — 'Take the same type as you took on your federal return.' The shipped standard_deduction applies only to standard-deduction filers. DC Code sec.47-1803.04(b) is quoted in the booklet: electing the federal standard deduction forces the DC standard deduction and bars DC itemized deductions, and vice versa; if one spouse's/registered domestic partner's net income is determined by itemizing on a separate return, NEITHER may take the standard deduction. Itemizers enter DC itemized deductions on Line 18 via Calculation F: DC does NOT allow a deduction for state and local income taxes, and if DC AGI exceeds $200,000 ($100,000 if married filing separately) the itemized deduction (other than medical/dental, investment-interest, and casualty/theft losses) is reduced by 5% of DC AGI over the threshold. ADDITIONAL STANDARD DEDUCTION for age/blindness NOT modeled: if you or your spouse/registered domestic partner were born before January 2, 1961, or are blind, an additional standard deduction of $1,600 per checkbox applies ($2,000 if single, head of household, or a dependent claimed by someone else and not married) — up from $1,550/$1,850 for 2024 — computed on Schedule S, Calculation G-1, which must be completed and submitted with the return. When married filing separately, the spouse boxes may be claimed only if the spouse had no gross income, is not filing, and cannot be claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer. DEPENDENT FILERS — 2025 SIMPLIFICATION: the income-dependent 'Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependent Filers' that the 2024 booklet used is GONE. For 2025 a dependent filer simply takes the $15,000 basic standard deduction ('$15,000 for single filers, dependent filers and married/registered domestic partner filers filing separately'; the Filing Requirements Chart likewise lists 'Dependent filer $15,000'), and Calculation G-1 adds only the age/blind amounts. So the shipped single/MFS amount is correct for a dependent filer too. MARRIED/REGISTERED DOMESTIC PARTNERS FILING SEPARATELY ON THE SAME RETURN not modeled: this combined-return status takes a combined $30,000 standard deduction and computes each person's tax separately using Calculation J on Schedule S (each spouse's separate federal AGI, additions, subtractions and deductions), then combines the result — per-couple math the engine does not reproduce. The engine's married_filing_separately models a separate-return MFS filer with the $15,000 standard deduction. REGISTERED DOMESTIC PARTNERS: DC allows registered domestic partners to file jointly (use married_filing_jointly, $30,000) or separately on the same return — statuses that do not exist federally. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE: DC's 'qualifying widow(er) with dependent child' status takes the same $30,000 standard deduction as married filing jointly and the same universal rate schedule, so the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping reproduces the correct tax. PART-YEAR RESIDENTS: must prorate the standard deduction (and credits) by days domiciled in DC divided by 365 — 2025 is NOT a leap year, so the divisor is 365 (booklet worked example: 71 days of residency / 365) — and subtract income received during the period of nonresidence. The shipped full-year standard_deduction amounts do not apply as-is to part-year filers. DC HEALTH CARE SHARED RESPONSIBILITY not modeled: Line 25 adds an individual-mandate payment (Schedule HSR, Part IV, Line 17) to Line 24, producing Line 26 'Total tax and DC Health Care Shared Responsibility.' The engine computes only Line 20 tax. (The Worksheet C-1 District Average Bronze Plan Premium amounts were updated for 2025.) CREDITS not modeled (they are credits against tax, not base reductions), and two changed materially for 2025: Line 21 credit for child and dependent care expenses (federal Form 2441 Line 9c x .32), Line 22 non-refundable credits from DC Schedule U (including the Calculation K out-of-state income tax credit), Line 27 DC EITC — NOW 100% of the federal EIC, up from 70%, with the childless-filer worksheet maximum raised to $649 (DC ceiling $30,941, investment-income limit $11,950) — Line 28 Schedule H homeowner/renter property tax credit (maximum raised to $1,425, AGI limits $66,000/$90,000), and Line 29 refundable Schedule U credits (including Schedule ELC, maximum raised to $1,200 per child). The DC Child Tax Credit is REPEALED for 2025. ROUNDING: the D-40 and Schedule I instruct dollars-only entries ('Dollars only, do not enter cents'); the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches for the Calculation I computation.
